chunks: Ali, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Suleyman, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Inform me about the pimp (qawwad), what is his hadd (penalty)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no hadd upon the pimp. Is it not that he is given wages for what he procures?' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, he merely joins the male and the female in unlawfulness.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'That is the one who joins the male and the female in unlawfulness?' So I said, 'He is that, may I be sacrificed for you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is whipped three-quarters of the hadd of the adulterer, seventy-five lashes, and he is exiled from the city in which he is.'

So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, so what is upon a man who pounces upon a woman and shaves her head?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is whipped painful lashes, and he is imprisoned in the prison of the Muslims until her hair grows back. So if it grows back, the mahr (dower) of his womenfolk is taken from him, and if it does not grow back, the complete diya (blood money) of five thousand dirhams is taken from him.'

So I said, 'So how did it become the mahr of his womenfolk if her hair grows back?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'O Ibn Sinan! The hair of the woman and her virginity share in the beauty. So if one of the two is taken away, the complete mahr is obligatory for her.'
ai.seo_question: What is the hadd penalty for a pimp and the compensation for shaving a woman's head in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the pimp (qawwad) is not subject to a fixed hadd but receives ta'zir punishment of seventy-five lashes and exile, distinguishing him from the adulterer. For the man who forcibly shaves a woman's head, the Imam prescribes imprisonment until hair regrowth, with compensation determined by whether the hair returns, highlighting the scholarly view that a woman's hair and virginity are integral components of her beauty and value (mahr).
